messages.subject: Kendall tau - version discrepancy?
parts:
I would like to know if anyone has an explanation for the discrepancy
between these 2 runs.

Thanks,
Wil

> X <- c(68,70,71,71,72,77,77,86,87,88,91,91)
> Y <- c(64,65,77,80,72,65,76,88,72,81,90,96)
> cor.test(X,Y, method="k")

messages.subject: Re: Kendall tau - version discrepancy?
parts:
What version of R had you used for the initial results?

In the explanations of changes to R (https://svn.r-project.org/R/trunk/NEWS
), I noticed that for R version 2.2.0 (6 Oct 2005), it says:

o The nonparametric variants of cor.test() now behave better in
the presence of ties. The "spearman" method uses the asymptotic
approximation in that case, and the "kendall" method likewise,
but adds a correction for ties (this is not necessary in the
Spearman case).

karl

messages.author: 2e31d4737c394aa8
messages.subject: Re: Kendall tau - version discrepancy?
parts:
Unfortunately, I don't know the source of the first example. I know it
was within the last few months.

The odd thing: The anonymous example actually produces the Kendall
value based on "Practical Nonparametric Statistics" by Conover (pp.
252 - 260, especially p. 257).

The excerpt you include is consistent with how I want cor.test to
work. However, the result I get in my example, is consistent with
Kendall without correcting for ties. The anonymous example produces a
value which specifically corrects for ties or corrects for ties in a
manner different from most procedures.

Regards,
Wil
